svg.title: Worldwide Identity Web: network-first architecture, revision 0.4
svg.desc: Target architecture, not a deployed system. Device-bound membership admits a client to an isolated WireGuard overlay. A separate control plane manages credentials, names and expiring peer leases. Native wiw services authorize requests end-to-end. An isolated, disabled-by-default transition gateway separates external internet traffic. The current repository only implements syntax validation and explicit denial stubs.
svg.text: Worldwide Identity Web
WIW / a separate logical network, not just another login application
DESIGN 0.4 / OFFLINE PREVIEW
CONTROL PLANE / PROPOSED, NOT IMPLEMENTED
Enrollment and membership
Supported passport / eID + holder verification
Scoped credential, device key, renewal and recovery
No raw identity documents sent to native services.
Admission and authenticated registry
Bind proof to a peer key; issue expiring leases
wiw.<domain> -> service key + operator + routes
Revocation, freshness, key rotation; no DNS fallback.
Federation and governance
Issuer/operator trust, appeals and incident response
Public infrastructure audit; no personal-data log
Privacy model, legal review and certification still open.
NATIVE MEMBERSHIP BOUNDARY / EACH SERVICE STILL AUTHORIZES ACCESS
Member device
WIW-aware client / OS network agent
Proof of possession at login
Separate trust store and browsing origins
Never interpret public DNS as WIW trust
Hardware keys reduce, not eliminate, misuse.
Federated overlay fabric
Unmodified WireGuard / encrypted peer links
Service-scoped routing; no default lateral access
Controller enforces lease expiry and revocation
Authenticated peers are not trusted applications
No passport verification on every packet.
Native websites and apps
wiw.example.com
Authenticated service node + application
Per-service proof and least-privilege access
Existing HTTP stacks behind WIW integration
No automatic reachability from public browsers.
tunnel
route
Native sessions: end-to-end TLS / QUIC + service authorization.
What the repository does now
Validates wiw hostname syntax
Returns explicit not-implemented errors
Keeps all network capabilities disabled
No enrollment, registry, tunnel or proxy is live.
EXPLICIT TRANSITION BOUNDARY / DISABLED IN PREVIEW
Isolated egress gateway
Admitted clients only; bounded destination policy
Preserve HTTPS; never forward WIW credentials
Outside content remains untrusted, not anonymous.
Existing internet
Ordinary sites and public onboarding
Optional public mirrors stay isolated
No unauthenticated route into native services.
egress
UNDERLAY: TODAY'S IP NETWORKS FIRST
Existing fiber, mobile and Wi-Fi carry encrypted traffic. Independent peering / links later; no physical independence is claimed.
Design limits: verified document != trustworthy person; no global uniqueness, guaranteed anonymity, DDoS immunity or post-quantum claim.
IP: Apache-2.0 code / CC-BY-4.0 documentation. Copyright retained; trademark clearance and patent freedom-to-operate are not established.
